# Give each concept one plain, descriptive name

Name each product concept with one familiar, descriptive noun and use that exact term everywhere it appears: UI, CLI, SDK, docs, and agent messages.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. People learn a product through its words. A familiar noun lets them understand a concept without a definition, and one term per concept keeps them from wondering whether two words mean two things.

## Prefer

- Choose words users already use for the thing, then describe rather than brand it, unless the feature needs to be recognized on its own.
- Use one term per concept, and never swap in synonyms for variety.
- When something is a variant or role of an existing object, keep the base noun and name only the role, so a related item stays a plain instance of the base object.
- Agree on naming criteria before brainstorming: unique among existing names, short, the right part of speech, and focused on what the user does.

## Avoid

- Internal, implementation, or invented terms in user-facing copy.
- Two words for one concept, or one word for two concepts.
- Creative or branded names where a plain description works.

## Use when

- Naming a new feature, object, role, or relationship.
- Writing labels, navigation, settings, CLI flags, or docs that refer to product concepts.

## Do not use when

- A distinctive brand name is a deliberate product decision, such as a product or plugin name.

## Sources

- Nielsen Norman Group: Match between the system and the real world (usability heuristic #2) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/match-system-real-world/
- Shopify Polaris: Naming — https://polaris-react.shopify.com/content/naming
- SAP Fiori: UX writing basics (controlled terminology) — https://www.sap.com/design-system/fiori-design-web/v1-145/foundations/writing-and-wording/ux-writing/ux-writing-guidelines/basics
- UX Content Collective: 3-step process to name a new feature — https://uxcontent.com/3-step-process-to-name-a-new-feature/

## Check

- Would a new user understand the name without a definition?
- Does the same concept use the same word on every surface?
- Does a role or variant keep its base noun instead of becoming a new object type?
